issues.legal_issue: A tenant who lacked notice of a pending rent-default eviction suit during the statutory application period may obtain the benefit of the special tenant-protection provision by applying after learning of the suit and complying with the court’s payment directions.
material_facts: An eviction suit for alleged rent default was pending when the amending ordinance took effect.
The tenant had no notice of the suit during the 30-day period for applying under the new provision and received the plaint only later.
After receiving notice, the tenant sought determination of any arrears and interest, and deposited the amount determined by the trial court within the time it allowed.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was entitled to the benefit of Section 13-A even though he could not apply within 30 days of the ordinance’s commencement because he did not know that the suit was pending.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13-A(a) and (b) of the Rajasthan Premises (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1950, given overriding effect, was intended to benefit all tenants in pending rent-default proceedings who had not been actually evicted and who paid the arrears, interest and costs as directed. Its application deadline could not be applied to demand the impossible of a tenant unaware of the suit. Statutory provisions should be construed to advance legislative purpose rather than defeat it, following the approach described in B.P. Khemka Pvt. Ltd. v. V.B.K. Bhowmick, [1987] 2 SCR 559, which referred to Madhav Rao Scindia v. Union of India, AIR 1971 SC 530, and Deputy Custodian v. Official Receiver, [1965] 1 SCR 220.

rule.if: pending_eviction_suit_for_rent_default and proceeding_pending_when_tenant_relief_became_available and tenant_lacked_notice_during_application_window and tenant_applied_after_learning_of_suit and tenant_paid_amount_determined_by_court

predicates.pending_eviction_suit_for_rent_default: A landlord had brought an eviction proceeding alleging that the tenant had failed to pay rent.
predicates.proceeding_pending_when_tenant_relief_be: The eviction proceeding was pending when a new tenant-protection measure took effect.
predicates.tenant_lacked_notice_during_application_: The tenant had not been informed of the proceeding during the period initially allowed for applying for relief.
predicates.tenant_applied_after_learning_of_suit: After learning of the proceeding, the tenant asked the court to determine any unpaid rent and related amounts.
predicates.tenant_paid_amount_determined_by_court: The tenant paid the amount the court determined was due within the time the court allowed.

issues.definition: When a rent-default eviction proceeding is pending, the tenant lacked notice during the application window, and the tenant applies and pays as directed after learning of the suit, the tenant receives protection from eviction for that default.

issues.legal_issue: A prior cured rent default does not disqualify a tenant from special protection in a pending rent-default eviction proceeding when the later shortfall was not knowingly or wilfully committed and the tenant paid the arrears determined by the court.
material_facts: In an earlier eviction suit, the tenant had obtained a determination of arrears and interest, deposited the amount, and the suit was dismissed.
The tenant continued depositing rent in court, but the landlord later brought another eviction suit alleging default.
The tenant said that any shortfall during the ensuing years was an oversight and asked the court to determine any arrears and interest.
The court determined an amount due, which the tenant deposited within the time allowed.
The Court found that the tenant had not knowingly and wilfully committed a second default.
issues.conclusion: The earlier default and the tenant’s earlier use of the statutory cure did not disentitle him to Section 13-A’s benefit; the later alleged default did not bar relief under the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13-A has overriding effect for suits and other proceedings pending when the amending ordinance was promulgated. Accordingly, the proviso to Section 13(6) of the amended Act did not prevent the tenant from claiming Section 13-A’s benefit merely because he had obtained relief for an earlier default. The Court also relied on the finding that the later shortfall was not a knowing and wilful default and that the tenant paid the court-determined arrears and interest.

rule.if: pending_eviction_suit_for_rent_default and prior_rent_default_cured_in_earlier_case and later_shortfall_was_not_knowing_or_wilful and tenant_paid_amount_determined_by_court

predicates.pending_eviction_suit_for_rent_default: A landlord had brought an eviction proceeding alleging that the tenant had failed to pay rent.
predicates.prior_rent_default_cured_in_earlier_case: In an earlier proceeding, the tenant paid the amount determined by the court for a rent default and obtained the benefit of that payment.
predicates.later_shortfall_was_not_knowing_or_wilfu: The later rent shortfall resulted from oversight or omission rather than a knowing and wilful failure to pay.
predicates.tenant_paid_amount_determined_by_court: The tenant paid the amount the court determined was due within the time the court allowed.

issues.definition: In a pending rent-default eviction proceeding, a previously cured default does not disqualify the tenant from special protection when the later shortfall was not knowing or wilful and the tenant paid the amount determined by the court.
